tip.cash: Money in the bank. Sales minus parts, rent and late-night development.
tip.brand: Brand (0–100). Good reviews push it up, and a strong brand sells every phone a little easier.
tip.fans: Fans pre-order at launch. Every well-reviewed phone wins a few more.
tip.date: Game time. At 1× a day takes 5 seconds.
tip.design: Design 0–10: material, thinness, screen-to-body, size, color and proportions – judged against what people expect this year.
tip.tech: Tech 0–10: chip, display, battery, camera, storage and RAM – judged against what the market expects this year.
tip.review: Where the critics will probably land (±0.5). Better reviews sell a lot more phones.
tip.unitCost: What one phone costs you: parts, plastic, assembly, box.
tip.price: Shelf price. Set to a fair value for now – you get to pick it once you have an office.
tip.margin: What you keep from each phone sold.
tip.devTime: Game days until the prototype works (you, alone, at a workbench).
tip.devCost: Parts and prototypes. Paid up front.
tip.weekly: Likely sales in the first weeks. The garage can hand-build 50 phones a week.

settings.title: Settings
settings.resetConfirm: Really? Your company will be gone.

office.rented: Welcome to the office! Research, marketing and real production are open.
office.label: Startup office

research.title: Research lab
research.none: Nothing in the lab. Pick something below – it keeps running while you’re away.
research.budgetHint: Money buys research speed: every {amount}/week adds 1 RP/day.

company.title: Company
company.overstock: Overstocked: ~{weeks} weeks of phones in the warehouse. Storage costs add up, and the phone ages while it waits.

launchSetup.title: Launch setup
launchSetup.credit: The bank finances {amount} of the production run.
launchSetup.tooPoor: Not enough cash – lower marketing or the event.
launchSetup.overhype: Careful: hype above what the phone delivers costs fans.
launchSetup.bigBatch: That’s a big run. Phones age fast – unsold stock loses value.
launchSetup.factoryHint: Your factory builds the stock. Pre-orders wait a day or two. Slide right to also buy a contract batch.

team.title: Team
team.ratesTip: Design · Tech · Software points per day (founder included)
team.qualityTip: Compared to what a phone team should know this year. Below zero costs review points.
team.qualityHint: Your team is behind the times. Train people or hire stronger applicants: sloppy builds cost review points.
team.payrollWarn: Payroll eats {pct}% of your weekly profit. Careful.
team.empty: Nobody here yet. Hire a designer, an engineer and a programmer: phones get built faster and better.
team.noApplicants: Nobody's applying right now. Next batch soon.
team.roleHint: Designers → design points · Engineers → tech · Programmers → software · Researchers → research · Marketing (office 2) → hype.
team.trainTip: Two weeks away, comes back better.
team.noSeats: Office is full. Upgrade it first.
team.needOffice2: Lab and studio need office level 2.

traitTip.perfectionist: −10% speed, counts more for build quality

daily.title: Daily
daily.calendarHint: Drop by once a day. Miss a day? No problem, your streak just waits.
daily.noOrders: Odd jobs show up once the clock is running.
daily.resetHint: New odd jobs every day at midnight.

loan.title: Bank loan
loan.auto: Each week the bank takes 25% of the profit, plus any cash above {reserve} (your safety reserve).

factory.title: Factory
factory.pitch: Stop paying the contract manufacturer's markup. Your own lines build phones cheaper, right when you need them.
factory.point1: No 20% markup, no 2-week wait, no minimum batch.
factory.point2: Lines keep a few weeks of stock and stop when the shelves are full.
factory.point3: Upgrade lines for speed and cheaper assembly. Watch the scrap rate: returns cost review points.
factory.locked: Unlocks at the phase-3 goal (valuation + brand).
factory.idle: Idle – tap to pick a phone
factory.cycleTip: Tap to switch which phone this line builds
factory.tooSlow: Customers want {demand}/wk. This line can't keep up: upgrade it or add a line.
factory.overflow: The warehouse is overflowing. Extra stock costs 1% of its value every week.
factory.howItWorks: New phones get a line automatically (an idle one, or the one building your weakest seller).
